title: Enoch Long's pocket journal, Tiverton and Newport, July 1779 - December 1780 (pension file W. 16138): a New Hampshire soldier's private alphabet of altered letters, changed on 4 October 1779 to a second alphabet he wrote out in the notebook; read in part

documents.shelfmark: NARA RG 15, Revolutionary War Pension and Bounty-Land Warrant Application File W. 16138 (Enoch Long, widow Molly), microfilm M804 roll 1580, catalog NAID 196199890, images 11-31
documents.route: private journal of Enoch Long, Capt. Samuel Runnels's company, Col. Hercules Mooney's New Hampshire regiment, Tiverton and Newport, Rhode Island

plaintext.source: No decipherment anywhere in the pension file; the clerk's wrapper (image 10) says only 'Journal partly written in Cipher'.

transcription.source: National Archives Catalog full-size JPEGs (the largest the catalog serves; byte-identical to the 13 Nov download), line strips at 1.7-2.6x
transcription.notes: Signs counted by scripts/build_reconciled.py over reconciled words (the measure tool counts words or Latin letters only; 888 word tokens including 185 unread placeholders). Two passes: pass A (first agent, readings and a sign transcription of 15L-16L) and pass B (blind, shape codes, frozen before pass A was opened); reconciled line by line with both open. Microfilm x-height about 15 pixels; look-alike signs settled by context where the image alone does not.

plaintext.source: None. The 4 Oct 1779 entry opens with 25 signs in two rows and no letters; their letter values are inferred from alphabetical order (a-s, t-z, no j).

transcription.notes: Images 16R, 17L (= 18R inverted), 24L, 25L, 26. 147 word tokens including 38 unread placeholders.

system.summary: Simple substitution with word division, one altered letter form per letter, mixed word by word with plain English; a second alphabet from 4 October 1779, whose 25 signs the writer set out in two rows at the head of that entry (letter values inferred from their order).
system.notes: System A has 21 signs settled (j, k, q, x, z rare or unseen; o also stands for u in up, but, upper). System B key line: 18 signs for a-s and 7 for t-z; on the microfilm e, n and z are all dashes, m and w both m-shaped, r and s both ezh-shaped. distinct_symbols unknown because some look-alike signs cannot be told apart on the film.

solution.what: Andrew Beling contribution, with AI agents: the Fold3 sweep flagged the wrapper note 'Journal partly written in Cipher' on file W. 16138; all 57 images downloaded from the National Archives Catalog.

Pass A: system A key recovered from plain-cipher mixtures ('Last [night]', 'you may [read writing where] you could see none', 'countersign was Huntington') and word patterns; key frozen from images 11, 13R, 14L, 14R.
Pass A held-out test on 105 words of 15L-16L transcribed by the same agent: 84.8% dictionary words against a shuffled-key maximum of 26.7%. Caveat: the transcriber knew the key.
Pass B, blind: every cipher word of 17 page-sides transcribed as shape codes and frozen (sha256 f76fbb51...) before pass A's folder was opened; shape codes merge some look-alike signs.

Pass B blind key from the guard roster (plain 'Sergt Cate, Corpl Jonson', 'For Guard' above the same words in cipher) and plain-cipher mixtures: same letters as the frozen key for 15 letters once merges are split; f and v wrong.

Clean held-out test, written down first: frozen key on the blind pass B transcription of seven pages not used to build it, 409 words: 57.9% English against 200 shuffled keys (mean 11.4%, 99th percentile 23.0%, maximum 30.3%). Pass.

System B: the first two lines of the 4 October 1779 entry read as Long's own alphabet (a-s, t-z); checked against last night, I dreamed, that I was at home, thought, Kimballs, followed, furlough; key frozen (sha256 1a449ea4...).

Line-by-line reconciliation on line strips of the full-size catalog images with both keys and both passes open; every cipher word recorded with pass A, pass B, signs, decoded word and a confidence mark; nonsense left as nonsense. Settled: 'dreaming' and 'father was come to us' on 14R (pass A right), the invisible-ink passage word by word, the name read as Polly (p sign, not m), new readings on image 11, 15L, 16L ('white ink') and 22L.

HathiTrust full text, Google Books, Internet Archive, NH Historical Society catalogue, Southern Campaigns pension statements, genealogy sites; NH State Papers rolls and Lord's Hopkinton history read for context: no prior transcription or mention of the cipher.

Statistical validation (docs/_validate.py): 1494 tokens, 21 types, en-modern order 4: reading -1.743 per letter; random keys -7.027 (z 8.6); key annealed onto shuffled ciphertext best -4.779 (mean -4.824, z 55.4); annealer on the real text -1.743. Verdict: pass.

A second AI agent solved system A from the images before seeing the key (all 21 letters agree), compared 45 words read by both (43 agree), and reran both held-out tests and _validate.py with identical results. Its corrections applied: eyes (not soul), again, dress'd up in a silk gown, yesterday, to bed; alphabet line described as signs with values inferred from order; Polly evidence restated.

Better images sought: the National Archives Catalog IIIF service gives 2064 x 2689 pixels at full/max, pixel for pixel the same as the JPG already held (image 16 checked); Fold3's viewer shows the same scan, no sharper. Lower-case letters stay about 15 pixels high.

Blind second reading: eight Opus agents, given only the sign chart and 235 line crops in shuffled order (no earlier reading), transcribed every cipher word sign by sign (plan written and hashed first: output/long1779_accuracy_2026-11-15/TEST_PLAN_blind.md). Sign for sign they agreed with 399 of 721 earlier confident words (55%); with 29 of a fixed sample of 60 (48%, against a pass mark of 95%); with 4 of 24 probable and 8 of 60 doubtful words. Where lengths matched, 86% of signs agreed in the first alphabet and 75% in the second.

Every disagreement and every weak word (663 items) judged on the image by eight further Opus agents, shown the two readings in random order; the worker then checked the private passages and every name on the image. Rules: confident only if two readings agree sign for sign, or the signs are individually clear, and the word fits; otherwise probable, doubtful or unread. Result: 513 confident, 262 probable, 60 doubtful, 206 unread of 1,041. Changed: 'sentinel' is 'century' (sentry); 'mother' and 'married' (6 Oct) are not on the signs; 'whipt' (22 Aug) is not on the image, the man had to 'run the [gantlet??] through the company'; on 16R the name is not Polly on the signs; Kimball's first sign is the s sign; 'Hannah' read on 16L. A curl sign in 'ink' and 'silk' is probably the first alphabet's k.
